briefdescription.para: Initializes a XCanPs instance/driver.

detaileddescription.para: Provides core driver functions from xcanps.c.

The initialization entails:
Initialize all members of the XCanPs structure.
Reset the CAN device. The CAN device enters Configuration Mode immediately after the reset finishes.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanPs device configuration structure.

Device base address in the virtual memory address space. If the address translation is not used then the physical address is passed. Unexpected errors may occur if the address mapping changes after this function is invoked.

simplesect.para: XST_SUCCESS always.

briefdescription.para: Resets the CAN device.

detaileddescription.para: Calling this function resets the device immediately, and any pending transmission or reception terminates at once. Both Object Layer and Transfer Layer are reset. This function does not reset the Physical Layer. All registers are reset to the default values, and no previous status is restored. TX FIFO, RX FIFO and TX High Priority Buffer are also reset.

When an internal error requires a reset, the driver notifies the upper layer software through the error status code or interrupts. The upper layer software is responsible for calling this Reset function and then re-configuring the device.
The CAN device enters Configuration Mode immediately after this function returns.

briefdescription.para: Returns the current operation mode of the CAN device.

listitem.para: XCANPS_MODE_CONFIG if the device is in Configuration Mode.
XCANPS_MODE_SLEEP if the device is in Sleep Mode.
XCANPS_MODE_NORMAL if the device is in Normal Mode.
XCANPS_MODE_LOOPBACK if the device is in Loop Back Mode.
XCANPS_MODE_SNOOP if the device is in Snoop Mode.

briefdescription.para: Enters the specified CAN operation mode.

detaileddescription.para:
Allows the CAN device to enter one of the following operation modes:
Configuration Mode: Pass in parameter XCANPS_MODE_CONFIG
Sleep Mode: Pass in parameter XCANPS_MODE_SLEEP
Normal Mode: Pass in parameter XCANPS_MODE_NORMAL
Loop Back Mode: Pass in parameter XCANPS_MODE_LOOPBACK.
Snoop Mode: Pass in parameter XCANPS_MODE_SNOOP.
Read the xcanps.h file and device specification for detailed description of each operation mode.

parameterdescription.para: Specify which operation mode to enter. Valid value is any of XCANPS_MODE_* defined in xcanps.h. Multiple modes cannot be entered at the same time.

simplesect.para: This function does NOT ensure CAN device enters the specified operation mode before it returns the control to the caller. The caller is responsible for checking current operation mode using XCanPs_GetMode().

detaileddescription.para: Use the XCANPS_SR_* constants defined in xcanps_hw.h to interpret the returned value.

simplesect.para: The 32-bit value read from Status Register.

simplesect.para: The 32-bit value read from Error Status Register.

briefdescription.para: Clears Error Status bits previously set in Error Status Register (ESR).

detaileddescription.para: Use the XCANPS_ESR_* constants defined in xcanps_hw.h to create the value to pass in. If a bit was cleared in Error Status Register before this function is called, it is not modified.

parameterdescription.para: 32-bit mask used to clear bits in Error Status Register. A bitwise OR of multiple XCANPS_ESR_* values clears multiple bits.

briefdescription.para: Sends a CAN Frame.

detaileddescription.para: If the TX FIFO is not full then the given frame is written into the TX FIFO; otherwise, it returns an error code immediately. This function does not wait for the given frame to be sent to the CAN bus.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to a 32-bit aligned buffer containing the CAN frame to be sent.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if TX FIFO was not full and the given frame was written into the FIFO.
XST_FIFO_NO_ROOM if there is no room in the TX FIFO for the given frame.
XST_DEVICE_BUSY if a transfer is already in progress.

briefdescription.para: Receives a CAN Frame.

detaileddescription.para: This function first checks if RX FIFO is empty; if not, it then reads a frame from the RX FIFO into the given buffer. This function returns an error code immediately if there is no frame in the RX FIFO.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to a 32-bit aligned buffer where the CAN frame is written.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if RX FIFO was not empty and a frame was read from RX FIFO successfully and written into the given buffer.
XST_NO_DATA if there is no frame to be received from the FIFO.

briefdescription.para: Sends a CAN High Priority frame.

detaileddescription.para: This function first checks if TX High Priority Buffer is empty. If yes, it then writes the given frame into the Buffer. If not, this function returns immediately. This function does not wait for the given frame to be sent to the CAN bus.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to a 32-bit aligned buffer containing the CAN High Priority frame to be sent.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if TX High Priority Buffer was not full and the given frame was written into the buffer.
XST_FIFO_NO_ROOM if there is no room in the TX High Priority Buffer for this frame.
XST_DEVICE_BUSY if a transfer is already in progress.

simplesect.para: To send the frame immediately, without a delay from processor interrupt handling, disable interrupts at the processor level before invoking this function.

briefdescription.para: Enables individual acceptance filters.

detaileddescription.para: Up to 4 filters can be enabled.

parameterdescription.para: Specifies which filters to enable. Use any XCANPS_AFR_UAF*_MASK to enable one filter, and combine multiple XCANPS_AFR_UAF*_MASK values if multiple filters need to be enabled. Any filter not specified in this parameter keeps its previous enable/disable setting.

briefdescription.para: Disables individual acceptance filters.

detaileddescription.para: Up to 4 filters can be disabled. If all acceptance filters are disabled then all the received frames are stored in the RX FIFO.

parameterdescription.para: Specifies which filters to disable. Use any XCANPS_AFR_UAF*_MASK to disable one filter, and combine multiple XCANPS_AFR_UAF*_MASK values if multiple filters need to be disabled. Any filter not specified in this parameter keeps its previous enable/disable setting. If all acceptance filters are disabled then all received frames are stored in the RX FIFO.

briefdescription.para: Returns enabled acceptance filters.

detaileddescription.para: Use XCANPS_AFR_UAF*_MASK defined in xcanps_hw.h to interpret the returned value. If no acceptance filters are enabled then all received frames are stored in the RX FIFO.

simplesect.para: The value stored in Acceptance Filter Register.

memberdef.name: XCanPs_AcceptFilterSet

briefdescription.para: Sets values to the Acceptance Filter Mask and ID Registers.

detaileddescription.para: Sets values to the Acceptance Filter Mask Register (AFMR) and Acceptance Filter ID Register (AFIR) for the specified Acceptance Filter. Use XCANPS_IDR_* defined in xcanps_hw.h to create the values to set the filter. Read the xcanps.h file and device specification for details.

This function should be called only after:
The given filter is disabled by calling XCanPs_AcceptFilterDisable().
And the CAN device is ready to accept writes to AFMR and AFIR, that is, XCanPs_IsAcceptFilterBusy() returns FALSE.

parameterdescription.para: Defines which Acceptance Filter Mask and ID Register to set. Use any single XCANPS_AFR_UAF*_MASK value.
Value to write to the chosen Acceptance Filter Mask Register.
Value to write to the chosen Acceptance Filter ID Register.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if the values were set successfully.
XST_FAILURE if the given filter was not disabled, or the CAN device was not ready to accept writes to AFMR and AFIR.

briefdescription.para: Reads the Acceptance Filter Mask and ID Register values.

detaileddescription.para: Reads the values of the Acceptance Filter Mask and ID Register for the specified Acceptance Filter. Use XCANPS_IDR_* defined in xcanps_hw.h to interpret the values. Read the xcanps.h file and device specification for details.

parameterdescription.para: Defines which Acceptance Filter Mask Register to get Mask and ID from. Use any single XCANPS_FILTER_* value.
Pointer to the data in which the Mask value read from the chosen Acceptance Filter Mask Register is returned.
Pointer to the data in which the ID value read from the chosen Acceptance Filter ID Register is returned.

briefdescription.para: Sets the Baud Rate Prescaler value.

detaileddescription.para: The system clock for the CAN controller is divided by (Prescaler + 1) to generate the quantum clock needed for sampling and synchronization. Read the device specification for details.
Baud Rate Prescaler can be set only if the CAN device is in Configuration Mode. Call XCanPs_EnterMode() to enter Configuration Mode before using this function.

parameterdescription.para: Value to set. Valid values are from 0 to 255.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if the Baud Rate Prescaler value is set successfully.
XST_FAILURE if CAN device is not in Configuration Mode.

briefdescription.para: Gets the Baud Rate Prescaler value.

detaileddescription.para: The system clock for the CAN controller is divided by (Prescaler + 1) to generate the quantum clock needed for sampling and synchronization. Read the device specification for details.

simplesect.para: Current used Baud Rate Prescaler value. The value's range is from 0 to 255.

detaileddescription.para: Time segment 1, Time segment 2 and Synchronization Jump Width are set in this function. Device specification requires the values passed into this function be one less than the actual values of these fields. Read the device specification for details.
Bit time can be set only if the CAN device is in Configuration Mode. Call XCanPs_EnterMode() to enter Configuration Mode before using this function.

Time Segment 2 value to set. Valid values are from 0 to 7.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if the Bit time is set successfully.
XST_FAILURE if CAN device is not in Configuration Mode.

briefdescription.para: Gets the Bit time parameters.

detaileddescription.para: Time segment 1, Time segment 2 and Synchronization Jump Width values are read in this function. According to device specification, the actual value of each of these fields is one more than the value read. Read the device specification for details.

Time Segment 2 value after this function returns. Its value ranges from 0 to 7.
Time Segment 1 value after this function returns. Its value ranges from 0 to 15.

briefdescription.para: Provides diagnostic self-test functions from xcanps_selftest.c.

detaileddescription.para: Runs a self-test on the CAN driver and device.
The test resets the device and sets up the Loop Back mode. It then sends a standard frame, receives the frame, verifies the contents, and resets the device again.
Note that this is a destructive test in that resets of the device are performed. Refer the device specification for the device status after the reset operation.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS if the self-test passed, that is, the frame received via the internal loop back has the same contents as the frame sent.
XST_FAILURE otherwise.

simplesect.para:
If the CAN device does not work properly, this function may enter an infinite loop and never returns to the caller.
If XST_FAILURE is returned, the device is not reset so that the caller could have a chance to check the reasons causing the failure.

briefdescription.para: Provides interrupt-related functions from xcanps_intr.c.

detaileddescription.para: Enables the specified interrupts.
Use the XCANPS_IXR_* constants defined in xcanps_hw.h to create the bit-mask to enable interrupts.

parameterdescription.para: Mask to enable. Bit positions of 1 are enabled. Bit positions of 0 keep the previous setting. This mask is formed by a bitwise OR of XCANPS_IXR_* bits defined in xcanps_hw.h.

briefdescription.para: Disables the specified interrupts.

detaileddescription.para: Use the XCANPS_IXR_* constants defined in xcanps_hw.h to create the bit-mask to disable interrupts.

parameterdescription.para: Mask to disable. Bit positions of 1 are disabled. Bit positions of 0 keep the previous setting. This mask is formed by a bitwise OR of XCANPS_IXR_* bits defined in xcanps_hw.h.

briefdescription.para: Returns the currently enabled interrupts.

detaileddescription.para: Use the XCANPS_IXR_* constants defined in xcanps_hw.h to interpret the returned value.

simplesect.para: Enabled interrupts in a 32-bit format.

briefdescription.para: Returns the interrupt status.

detaileddescription.para: Reads the Interrupt Status Register. Use the XCANPS_IXR_* constants defined in xcanps_hw.h to interpret the returned value.

simplesect.para: The value stored in Interrupt Status Register.

briefdescription.para: Clears the specified interrupts.

detaileddescription.para: Every bit set in Interrupt Status Register indicates that a specific type of interrupt is occurring. This function clears one or more interrupts by writing a bit mask to Interrupt Clear Register.

parameterdescription.para: Mask to clear. Bit positions of 1 are cleared. Bit positions of 0 do not change the previous interrupt status. This mask is formed by a bitwise OR of XCANPS_IXR_* bits defined in xcanps_hw.h.

briefdescription.para: Handles CAN interrupts.

detaileddescription.para: This handler reads the interrupt status from the ISR, determines the source of the interrupts, calls according callbacks, and finally clears the interrupts.

The application beyond this driver is responsible for providing callbacks to handle interrupts and installing the callbacks using XCanPs_SetHandler() during initialization phase. An example delivered with this driver demonstrates how this could be done.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the XCanPs instance that just interrupted.

briefdescription.para: Installs an asynchronous callback function.

detaileddescription.para: Installs a callback for the given HandlerType:

para.preformatted: HandlerType Callback Function Type ----------------------- ------------------------ XCANPS_HANDLER_SEND XCanPs_SendRecvHandler XCANPS_HANDLER_RECV XCanPs_SendRecvHandler XCANPS_HANDLER_ERROR XCanPs_ErrorHandler XCANPS_HANDLER_EVENT XCanPs_EventHandler

HandlerType Invoked by this driver when: ------------------------------------------------------------------------- XCANPS_HANDLER_SEND A frame transmitted by a call to XCanPs_Send() has been sent successfully.
XCANPS_HANDLER_RECV A frame has been received and is sitting in the RX FIFO.
XCANPS_HANDLER_ERROR An error interrupt is occurring.
XCANPS_HANDLER_EVENT Any other kind of interrupt is occurring.

parameterdescription.para: Specifies which handler is to be attached.
User data item that is passed to the callback function when it is invoked.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS when handler is installed.
XST_INVALID_PARAM when HandlerType is invalid.

simplesect.para: Invoking this function for a handler that already has been installed replaces it with the new handler.

briefdescription.para: Provides static initialization functions from xcanps_sinit.c.

detaileddescription.para: Looks up the device configuration based on the unique device ID or base address.
The XCanPs_ConfigTable[] contains the configuration info for each device in the system.

parameterdescription.para: Contains the base address of the device.

simplesect.para: A pointer to the configuration found or NULL if the specified device ID or base address was not found. See xcanps.h for the definition of XCanPs_Config.
In XSCT/classic flow, DeviceId is used to look up the device configuration.
